description: Ten-panel composite figure on the low-density nano-bainitic Al–C steels S1, S2 and S3, mixing seven SEM micrographs (a–g), two light-optical micrographs (h, i) and one EDX table (j). (a) S1, 300 °C, 500 nm bar: fine aligned needle/lath bainite with arrows to (Fe,M)xCy. (b) S1, 350 °C, 1 µm bar, plus a 1 µm inset labelled "Spec.1 (Fe,M)xCy"; arrows 1, 2, 3 mark type 1 nB, type 2 nB and blocky γr. (c) S2, 300 °C, 200 nm bar, annotated "Spec.3 + (Fe,M)xCy". (d) S2, 350 °C, 1 µm, coarser sheaves, labels 1–3 and a (Fe,M)xCy inset. (e) S3, 350 °C, 5 µm, labels 3, 4 (impingement of bainite sheaves), 5 (αp). (f) S3, 270 °C, 5 µm, labels 4, 5, 6 (sluggish γr) and (Fe,M)xCy near a grain-boundary junction. (g) S3, 270 °C EDX-target SEM, 5 µm, with Spec.4 (AlN), Spec.5, Spec.6. (h, i) LOM of S3, 270 °C at Bt = 25,200 s and 43,200 s (100 µm bars; 50 µm black-background insets). (j) EDX table (C, N, Al, Si, Mn, Fe, Mo) for Spec.1–3 and Spec.4–6; grey cells mark the over-stoichiometric threshold. The figure shows that higher-Al S3 develops coarser αp plus blocky/sluggish γr and AlN, while S1 yields fine nano-bainite.

subfigures.description: SEM of steel S1 austempered at 300 °C, 500 nm scale bar; fine parallel needle/lath bainitic structure with white arrows pointing to features labelled (Fe,M)xCy.
SEM of S1 at 350 °C, 1 µm scale bar, with arrows numbered 1, 2 and 3 and a boxed inset labelled 'Spec.2 (Fe,M)xCy'; the inset itself is labelled 'Spec.1 (Fe,M)xCy' with a 1 µm scale bar.
SEM of S2 at 300 °C, 200 nm scale bar, a lath/needle matrix annotated 'Spec.3 + (Fe,M)xCy' with arrow 3.
SEM of S2 at 350 °C, 1 µm scale bar; coarser sheaves/plates with labels 1, 2, 3 and a dark inset region labelled (Fe,M)xCy.
SEM of S3 at 350 °C, 5 µm scale bar; mixed lath and blocky structure with labels 3, 4 and 5; a small inset in the lower-left corner whose scale value is not legible.
SEM of S3 at 270 °C, 5 µm scale bar; lenticular sheaves together with dark blocky regions and a large precipitate at a grain-boundary triple junction, labelled 4, 5, 6 and (Fe,M)xCy.
SEM of S3 at 270 °C used for EDX targeting, 5 µm scale bar; arrows point to particles labelled Spec.5, Spec.4 and Spec.6.
Light-optical micrograph (LOM) of S3 at 270 °C, Bt = 25,200 s, 100 µm scale bar, with a black-background inset (50 µm bar) showing bright irregular regions in the same field.
LOM of S3 at 270 °C, Bt = 43,200 s, 100 µm scale bar, again with a 50 µm black-background inset showing bright regions.

EDX composition table with rows C, N, Al, Si, Mn, Fe, Mo and columns Spec.1–Spec.3 (group 'S1&S2', all labelled (Fe,M)xCy) and Spec.4 (AlN), Spec.5, Spec.6 (group 'S3'); a side legend defines arrows 1–6 and the grey over-stoichiometric threshold shading.

observations.observation: (a) is an SEM micrograph of steel S1 after austempering at 300 °C with a 500 nm scale bar, showing a fine parallel needle-like bainitic morphology with white arrows pointing to features labelled (Fe,M)xCy.
(c) carries the shortest scale bar of the SEM panels, 200 nm, and is annotated 'Spec.3 + (Fe,M)xCy'.
Panel (b) contains a boxed inset micrograph labelled 'Spec.1 (Fe,M)xCy' that has its own 1 µm scale bar, while the main field is labelled 'Spec.2 (Fe,M)xCy'.

A legend printed to the right of table (j) defines the numbered arrows: 1 = type 1 nB, 2 = type 2 nB, 3 = blocky γr, 4 = impingement of bainite sheav[es], 5 = αp, 6 = sluggish γr, and the grey swatch = over-stoichiometric threshold.

Table (j) lists elements C, N, Al, Si, Mn, Fe, Mo for Spec.1, Spec.2, Spec.3 (grouped as 'S1&S2', each annotated (Fe,M)xCy) and Spec.4 (AlN), Spec.5, Spec.6 (grouped as 'S3'; Spec.5 and Spec.6 annotated (Fe,M)xCy).
In table (j) the carbon values are 16.1, 14.4 and 15.1 for Spec.1–Spec.3 and 6.9, 14.2 and 14.1 for Spec.4–Spec.6.
Only Spec.4 contains nitrogen (10.3) and it also has the highest Al (20.6) and the lowest Fe (60.8) of the table, consistent with its AlN designation.
Several table cells are shaded grey (notably the carbon row and the Spec.4 column), the shading being defined by the adjacent legend as the over-stoichiometric threshold.
Panels (h) and (i) are light-optical micrographs with 100 µm scale bars and each also contains a black-background inset with a 50 µm scale bar showing bright irregular regions of the same field.
The caption states that (h) is LOM for S3, T = 270 °C with Bt = 25,200 s, and (i) is S3, T = 270 °C with Bt = 43,200 s.
The caption states that table (j) reports EDX analyses taken from the locations shown in panels (b), (c) and (g).
The caption note states that due to EDX limitations in carbon measurement, carbon content was only considered to detect (Fe,M)xCy.

The citing abstract states that in steels with ≥6 wt.% Al the fastest transformation was for S1 at 350 °C with a transformation time of 1600 s, whereas for S3 (8.08 wt.% Al) the transformation time ranged from 14,000 to 43,000 s, matching the long Bt values of panels (h) and (i).
